details:
ORBIT – Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer

ORBIT is an interactive, browser-based educational platform designed to introduce children aged 7–12 to the fundamentals of space exploration and astronaut training.

What does the project do and how does it work?

ORBIT allows young learners to experience a simulated astronaut mission to the Moon or Mars. Players create an astronaut profile, select their destination, and manage essential resources such as oxygen, water, food, and power.

During the mission, players make decisions to maintain their resources and complete their journey successfully. Interactive challenges introduce important space concepts, including radiation safety and communication delays. The project also uses NASA's DONKI API to display real space-weather notifications.

What are the benefits?

  • Makes space science interesting and interactive for children.
  • Helps learners understand the challenges astronauts face during space missions.
  • Develops decision-making and problem-solving skills.
  • Teaches resource management and the importance of balancing limited supplies.
  • Introduces real space-weather information through NASA data.

What is the intended impact?

The main goal of ORBIT is to make space science more accessible, enjoyable, and easier to understand for young learners. It aims to encourage curiosity about the universe and inspire children to explore science, technology, and future space careers through interactive learning.

What tools and technologies were used?

The project was developed using:

  • HTML – To create the structure of the website.
  • CSS – To design the interface and space-themed appearance.
  • JavaScript – To implement mission activities, resource management, and interactive challenges.
  • NASA DONKI API – To retrieve real space-weather notifications.
  • Visual Studio Code – For writing and editing the code.
  • Netlify – For hosting the live website.
  • GitHub – For storing and managing the project source code.

How is the project creative?

ORBIT transforms space education into an interactive mission experience. Instead of simply reading about astronauts, children take the role of an astronaut and make decisions that affect their mission. Combining resource-management gameplay, radiation safety activities, communication challenges, and real NASA space-weather information makes learning more engaging.

What factors did we consider?

We considered the target age group, ease of use, simple navigation, visual appeal, educational value, and the importance of making the activities understandable for beginners. We also considered the limited resources available during space missions and designed simplified scenarios to demonstrate the importance of making careful decisions. Real NASA information is presented separately from simulated gameplay to avoid confusion.

ORBIT aims to turn curiosity about space into an engaging learning experience, helping the next generation discover the excitement of space exploration.
